scopeNote: Training-oriented generic transport-aircraft architecture. ATA chapter placement, equipment count, redundancy and exact installation zone vary by aircraft type and configuration; this atlas must not be used as an AMM, FCOM, MEL or certification substitute.

equipment.name: Air Conditioning Pack — Left
equipment.purpose: Cools and conditions bleed or compressed air before cabin distribution.
equipment.redundancy: Normally one of two independent packs; the remaining pack can provide degraded environmental control on many transport designs.
equipment.failureEffect: Single-pack loss usually produces reduced cooling/pressurization margin; dispatch and altitude limits are type/MEL dependent.

equipment.name: Air Conditioning Pack — Right
equipment.purpose: Provides the second conditioned-air path for cabin and cockpit environmental control.
equipment.redundancy: Paired architecture with the opposite-side pack on common twin-aisle/single-aisle transports.
equipment.failureEffect: Remaining pack normally carries reduced-demand operation; exact operational restrictions are aircraft-specific.

equipment.name: Air Cycle Machine
equipment.purpose: Uses compressor/turbine stages and heat exchangers to cool pack airflow without refrigerant.
equipment.redundancy: Usually one ACM within each pack; redundancy is achieved at pack level rather than within one ACM.
equipment.failureEffect: Affected pack may shut down or lose cooling capability.

equipment.name: Cabin Pressure Controller
equipment.purpose: Computes pressurization schedule and commands the outflow valve to regulate cabin altitude and differential pressure.
equipment.redundancy: Common architecture uses two independent or cross-monitoring controllers with automatic/manual fallback.
equipment.failureEffect: One controller can often be replaced by the standby channel; multiple failures can require manual pressurization or operational restrictions.

equipment.name: Outflow Valve
equipment.location: Aft pressure shell / lower aft fuselage
equipment.purpose: Meters cabin exhaust airflow to control cabin pressure.
equipment.redundancy: Typically one valve with redundant actuation/control paths or a manual backup mode; architecture varies.
equipment.failureEffect: Loss of automatic control can drive manual control or depressurization procedures depending on valve failure position.

equipment.name: Cabin Recirculation Fans
equipment.purpose: Recirculates filtered cabin air to reduce pack demand and improve air mixing.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple fans are commonly installed; partial fan loss normally reduces efficiency rather than causing immediate loss of ventilation.
equipment.failureEffect: Reduced recirculation and increased pack load; usually non-catastrophic.

equipment.name: Autopilot / Flight Director Computer
equipment.purpose: Computes autopilot and flight-director commands using navigation, air-data and pilot mode selections.
equipment.redundancy: Transport aircraft commonly use multiple flight-control/autoflight computing lanes; exact voting and engagement logic is type-specific.
equipment.failureEffect: One channel failure normally leaves reduced autopilot capability; multiple failures can force manual flight.

equipment.name: Mode Control Panel / Flight Control Unit
equipment.purpose: Allows crew selection of speed, heading/track, altitude, vertical modes and autopilot/flight-director modes.
equipment.redundancy: Physical control panel may contain dual channels or alternate FMS/manual control paths depending on design.
equipment.failureEffect: Can remove selected autoflight functions; alternate control or manual flight remains depending on architecture.

equipment.name: VHF Communication Transceivers
equipment.location: Avionics racks with antennas on fuselage
equipment.purpose: Provides line-of-sight voice/data communication with ATC and airline stations.
equipment.redundancy: Two or three VHF transceivers are common, with separate antennas/audio routing.
equipment.failureEffect: Loss of one radio normally leaves alternate communication radios available.

equipment.name: Communications Management Unit
equipment.purpose: Routes ACARS/air-ground digital messages across VHF, SATCOM or other data links.
equipment.redundancy: May be dual or supported by alternate communication paths depending on aircraft.
equipment.failureEffect: Datalink capability can be degraded while basic voice communication remains.

equipment.name: Engine Integrated Drive Generator — Left
equipment.purpose: Generates regulated AC electrical power from engine mechanical power.
equipment.redundancy: One engine-driven source per engine; electrical buses can normally be reconfigured so one source powers multiple buses within limits.
equipment.failureEffect: Remaining generator and/or APU generator can support the network; load shedding may occur.

equipment.name: Engine Integrated Drive Generator — Right
equipment.purpose: Provides the second independent engine-driven main AC source.
equipment.redundancy: Paired with opposite engine generator plus auxiliary/emergency sources.
equipment.failureEffect: Electrical system reconfigures to remaining generation; multiple-source loss invokes emergency power architecture.

equipment.name: APU Generator
equipment.location: APU accessory gearbox in tail cone
equipment.purpose: Supplies electrical power on ground and can provide an alternate source in flight where approved.
equipment.redundancy: Acts as an independent backup to engine-driven generators; availability envelope is type-specific.
equipment.failureEffect: Reduces backup generation capability and may restrict dispatch or extended operations.

equipment.name: Transformer Rectifier Units
equipment.purpose: Converts AC power to DC for avionics, battery charging support and DC loads.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple TRUs commonly feed segregated DC buses with bus-tie capability.
equipment.failureEffect: DC buses can often be reconfigured; multiple TRU losses may shed DC loads.

equipment.name: Main Aircraft Battery
equipment.purpose: Provides stored DC energy for starting support, transient stabilization and emergency/standby loads.
equipment.redundancy: One or more batteries may be installed; battery is itself an emergency source rather than the normal primary source.
equipment.failureEffect: Reduces emergency endurance and can affect APU/start or dispatch capability.

equipment.name: Emergency Generator / RAT Electrical Path
equipment.location: Deployable RAT or emergency-generation installation; type-specific
equipment.purpose: Provides essential electrical power after loss of normal generation.
equipment.redundancy: Independent last-resort source; some aircraft use hydraulic RAT power feeding an emergency generator, others use different standby architecture.
equipment.powerSource: Ram air / hydraulic or dedicated emergency source
equipment.failureEffect: Loss becomes significant primarily when normal and auxiliary generation are also unavailable.

equipment.name: Engine Fire Detection Loops
equipment.purpose: Detects overheat/fire conditions in engine nacelle fire zones.
equipment.redundancy: Dual sensing loops are common so one loop can fail while preserving detection coverage.
equipment.failureEffect: Single-loop loss often leaves reduced but available detection; dual-loop loss removes automatic detection for that zone.

equipment.name: Engine Fire Extinguisher Bottles
equipment.location: Pylon, wing root or fuselage fire-extinguishing bottle bay depending on type
equipment.purpose: Stores and discharges extinguishing agent into an engine fire zone after crew command.
equipment.redundancy: Two-shot capability per engine or shared bottle architecture is common; exact plumbing varies.
equipment.failureEffect: Reduced or lost extinguishing capability for the affected engine zone.

equipment.name: Cargo Smoke Detectors
equipment.purpose: Detects smoke in cargo compartments and sends warning to flight crew.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple detectors or dual-loop sampling provides coverage and fault tolerance.
equipment.failureEffect: Reduced detection coverage can invoke dispatch restrictions; complete loss is safety significant.

equipment.name: Primary Flight Control Computers
equipment.purpose: Computes control-law commands and drives or commands actuators for primary flight controls.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple segregated computing lanes/channels with monitoring and reconfiguration are typical; exact architecture varies widely.
equipment.failureEffect: Single-computer loss is normally accommodated; multiple losses can degrade control laws or available surfaces.

equipment.name: Elevator Actuators / PCUs
equipment.purpose: Converts hydraulic/electrohydraulic command into elevator motion for pitch control.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple actuators and segregated hydraulic/electrical supplies are normally used across left/right elevator surfaces.
equipment.failureEffect: One actuator can be isolated while remaining actuators maintain pitch control; multiple correlated failures are much more severe.

equipment.name: Aileron Actuators / PCUs
equipment.purpose: Moves ailerons for roll control and trim augmentation.
equipment.redundancy: Left/right surfaces plus spoiler roll-control capability provide functional redundancy.
equipment.failureEffect: A single actuator/surface loss typically leaves roll authority through remaining aileron/spoilers.

equipment.name: Rudder Actuators / PCUs
equipment.purpose: Provides yaw control, engine-out compensation and coordination.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple PCUs/actuation channels and hydraulic sources are typical.
equipment.failureEffect: Single-channel loss is normally tolerated; further failures reduce yaw-control capability.

equipment.name: Flap Power Drive Unit
equipment.location: Wing center / flap drive transmission area
equipment.purpose: Provides mechanical drive to trailing-edge flap transmission and actuators.
equipment.redundancy: Dual hydraulic/electric motor paths or monitored drive channels are common; asymmetry protection is independent.
equipment.failureEffect: Flaps may stop at current position or move at reduced rate; asymmetry protection prevents hazardous differential motion.

equipment.name: Slat Power Drive Unit
equipment.purpose: Drives leading-edge slats for low-speed lift augmentation.
equipment.redundancy: Monitored dual drive paths and asymmetry protection are typical.
equipment.failureEffect: Slats can freeze in current configuration; landing/takeoff performance consequences are configuration-dependent.

equipment.name: Wing Tank Boost Pumps
equipment.purpose: Provides positive fuel pressure from tanks to engine feed manifolds.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple pumps per tank/side plus suction-feed capability on some aircraft provide fault tolerance.
equipment.failureEffect: One pump loss is usually tolerated; combinations can require crossfeed or suction feed and operational restrictions.

equipment.name: Fuel Crossfeed Valve
equipment.purpose: Connects left and right engine feed manifolds for balancing or feeding an engine from the opposite side.
equipment.redundancy: Single valve may provide system-level redundancy by allowing alternate tank/side feed paths.
equipment.failureEffect: Loss can reduce alternate feeding and balancing options.

equipment.name: Fuel Quantity Indicating System
equipment.purpose: Measures tank fuel quantity and supplies cockpit/maintenance indications.
equipment.redundancy: Uses multiple tank probes with computational compensation; independent low-level warnings may supplement quantity indication.
equipment.failureEffect: Quantity indication degradation can require conservative fuel procedures or dispatch restrictions.

equipment.name: Engine Driven Hydraulic Pumps
equipment.purpose: Provides primary hydraulic pressure while engines are running.
equipment.redundancy: Separate engine-driven pumps feed independent hydraulic systems; electric pumps and/or RAT backup essential functions.
equipment.failureEffect: Associated hydraulic system loses its main pump but can retain pressure from alternate/backup pumps depending on design.

equipment.name: Electric Motor Hydraulic Pumps
equipment.location: Main gear bay / center hydraulic equipment bay
equipment.purpose: Provides hydraulic pressure on ground and backs up engine-driven pumps in flight.
equipment.redundancy: Usually one or more electric pumps distributed across independent hydraulic systems.
equipment.failureEffect: Reduces backup hydraulic availability and can restrict dispatch.

equipment.name: Hydraulic Reservoirs
equipment.purpose: Stores, conditions and supplies hydraulic fluid to system pumps.
equipment.redundancy: Independent reservoirs are normally segregated by hydraulic system to prevent a single leak draining all systems.
equipment.failureEffect: Loss/leak can disable the associated hydraulic system while segregated systems remain available.

equipment.name: Wing Anti-Ice Valves
equipment.purpose: Controls hot bleed airflow to protected wing leading-edge sections.
equipment.redundancy: Left and right wings are normally independently controlled; bleed sources can often be cross-supplied.
outputs: Hot air to wing leading edge
equipment.failureEffect: Affected wing anti-ice capability can be lost or restricted; icing-condition operation becomes constrained.

equipment.name: Engine Nacelle Anti-Ice Valves
equipment.purpose: Routes hot compressor bleed air to engine inlet/nacelle anti-ice surfaces.
equipment.redundancy: Each engine has an independent anti-ice path; opposite engine does not normally anti-ice the failed engine inlet.
equipment.failureEffect: Affected engine inlet anti-ice can become unavailable, restricting operation in icing conditions.

equipment.name: Pitot / Static / AOA Heating
equipment.location: External air-data probes on forward fuselage
equipment.purpose: Prevents icing of flight-critical air-data sensors.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple independent probes each have dedicated heating and monitoring; air-data redundancy limits single-probe impact.
equipment.failureEffect: Affected probe can become unreliable in icing; remaining probes/computers provide alternate data if architecture permits.

equipment.name: Flight Data Recorder
equipment.purpose: Records required flight, system and engine parameters for accident investigation and operational monitoring.
equipment.redundancy: A single crash-protected recorder is common, although some aircraft use combined or deployable recorders.
equipment.failureEffect: No immediate flight-control effect, but recording capability is lost and dispatch requirements may apply.

equipment.name: Display Management Computers
equipment.purpose: Generates or manages data presented on primary/navigation/system cockpit displays.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple display computers and cross-side reversion modes are common.
equipment.failureEffect: One display channel can normally be reverted to another source; multiple failures reduce flight-deck display capability.

equipment.name: Central Warning / Alerting Computer
equipment.purpose: Consolidates system failures and generates prioritized crew alerts, cautions and warnings.
equipment.redundancy: Dual processing channels or distributed alerting paths are common on modern transports.
equipment.failureEffect: Loss of one channel normally leaves alternate alerting; multiple losses can significantly reduce crew awareness.

equipment.name: Landing Gear Control / Interface Unit
equipment.purpose: Controls or monitors landing-gear extension/retraction, position logic, door sequencing and air/ground status.
equipment.redundancy: Dual control/interface units or dual channels are common, with mechanical/gravity extension as alternate means.
equipment.failureEffect: Automatic normal gear operation may be lost; alternate/gravity extension remains on many designs.

equipment.name: Brake Control Unit
equipment.purpose: Commands normal braking, autobrake and anti-skid functions from pedal and wheel-speed inputs.
equipment.redundancy: Dual channels plus alternate/emergency braking and accumulator capability are typical.
equipment.failureEffect: Normal braking can degrade to alternate braking; anti-skid/autobrake may be lost depending on failure.

equipment.name: Brake Accumulator
equipment.purpose: Stores hydraulic energy for parking and/or emergency braking after normal hydraulic pressure loss.
equipment.redundancy: Provides an independent stored-energy backup to normal hydraulic brake supply.
equipment.failureEffect: Reduces emergency/parking brake endurance but normal hydraulic braking may remain.

equipment.name: Nose Wheel Steering Actuator / Control
equipment.purpose: Steers the nose wheel from tiller/pedal/autopilot inputs during ground operations.
equipment.redundancy: Mechanical free-caster/towing modes or alternate channels may exist; exact architecture varies.
equipment.failureEffect: Taxi maneuverability is reduced; differential braking may remain available.

equipment.name: Navigation / Strobe / Beacon Lights
equipment.location: Wing tips, tail and fuselage exterior
equipment.purpose: Provides aircraft position, anti-collision and recognition lighting.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple independent light units and circuits reduce single-point loss.
equipment.failureEffect: Operational/dispatch restrictions depend on which light and flight conditions are affected.

equipment.name: Air Data Inertial Reference Units
equipment.location: Forward avionics bay; remote air-data modules/sensors distributed forward
equipment.purpose: Provides attitude, heading, acceleration, airspeed, altitude and inertial/navigation reference data.
equipment.redundancy: Three independent reference channels are common on large transports, with source comparison/reversion logic.
equipment.failureEffect: One channel loss is normally tolerated; multiple disagreeing/lost channels progressively degrade navigation, displays and flight-control functions.

equipment.name: Flight Management Computers
equipment.purpose: Computes route, performance, guidance and navigation solutions using aircraft and database inputs.
equipment.redundancy: Dual FMCs or dual channels are common, with independent navigation sources and manual reversion.
equipment.failureEffect: One FMC loss generally leaves the other channel; total FMS loss requires conventional/manual navigation and performance management.

equipment.name: Multi-Mode Receiver / GNSS Receiver
equipment.location: Avionics bay with antennas on upper fuselage
equipment.purpose: Provides GNSS and often ILS/GLS navigation/approach reception.
equipment.redundancy: Two independent receivers/antenna paths are common for dispatch and approach integrity.
equipment.failureEffect: Single receiver loss reduces redundancy; alternate radio/inertial navigation may remain.

equipment.name: Radio Altimeters
equipment.location: Transmit/receive antennas on lower fuselage plus avionics units
equipment.purpose: Measures height above terrain at low altitude for flare, autoland, GPWS and other functions.
equipment.redundancy: Dual or triple radio-altimeter channels are common on autoland-capable aircraft.
equipment.failureEffect: Can remove autoland/low-visibility capability and degrade terrain/flare functions depending on remaining channels.

equipment.name: Weather Radar
equipment.location: Nose radome antenna with electronics in forward avionics area
equipment.purpose: Detects precipitation and weather reflectivity ahead of the aircraft.
equipment.redundancy: Often one radar antenna/system; strategic weather information and visual/ATC information provide operational alternatives but not equivalent onboard redundancy.
equipment.failureEffect: Crew loses onboard weather radar information; weather-operation restrictions apply.

equipment.name: Traffic Collision Avoidance System Computer
equipment.location: Avionics bay with top/bottom directional antennas
equipment.purpose: Tracks transponder-equipped traffic and generates traffic/resolution advisories.
equipment.redundancy: Usually a single TCAS computer with multiple antennas and independent aircraft surveillance/ATC layers; no full onboard duplicate is typical.
equipment.failureEffect: Loss of TCAS removes onboard collision-avoidance advisories; ATC separation remains a separate safety layer.

equipment.name: Mode S Transponders
equipment.purpose: Replies to secondary surveillance radar and supports ADS-B/TCAS surveillance functions.
equipment.redundancy: Two transponders are common, normally one active at a time.
equipment.failureEffect: Single transponder loss normally leaves the standby unit; total loss affects ATC surveillance and TCAS interoperability.

equipment.name: Crew Oxygen Cylinder & Regulators
equipment.purpose: Provides pressurized breathing oxygen to flight crew during smoke or depressurization events.
equipment.redundancy: Independent stored oxygen supply is separate from normal cabin-air system; cylinder/regulator redundancy depends on aircraft.
equipment.failureEffect: Loss is safety-significant for depressurization/smoke scenarios and normally has strict dispatch requirements.

equipment.name: Passenger Oxygen System
equipment.location: Passenger service units above seats; generators or centralized cylinders depending on design
equipment.purpose: Provides temporary passenger oxygen after cabin depressurization.
equipment.redundancy: Many independent chemical generators or distributed masks limit the effect of a single-unit failure.
equipment.failureEffect: Localized unit failure affects a seat group; system-wide deployment failure is highly safety significant.

equipment.name: Engine Bleed Pressure Regulating Valves
equipment.location: Engine compressor bleed / pylon pneumatic duct
equipment.purpose: Regulates engine bleed-air pressure and isolates the source when commanded or during faults.
equipment.redundancy: One bleed source per engine plus APU bleed and crossbleed manifold provide alternate supply paths.
equipment.failureEffect: One source loss can often be compensated by the opposite engine or APU within operating limits.

equipment.name: Crossbleed / Isolation Valve
equipment.location: Pneumatic manifold near wing-body center section
equipment.purpose: Connects or isolates left/right pneumatic manifolds for engine start, pack supply and fault isolation.
equipment.redundancy: Single isolation valve enables cross-side redundancy between otherwise separate pneumatic sources.
equipment.failureEffect: Can reduce cross-side supply and alternate engine-start/pack capability.

equipment.name: Potable Water Tank / Pump / Pressurization
equipment.purpose: Stores and distributes potable water to galleys and lavatories.
equipment.redundancy: Not normally safety-critical; redundancy focuses on isolation rather than duplicate complete systems.
equipment.failureEffect: Cabin-service degradation; flight safety impact is generally low.

equipment.name: Vacuum Waste System
equipment.location: Waste tank and vacuum equipment bay
equipment.purpose: Transfers lavatory waste to a sealed storage tank using pressure differential/vacuum.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple lavatories feed a common or segmented waste system; isolation valves localize faults.
equipment.failureEffect: Cabin-service restriction; affected lavatories may be locked out.

equipment.name: Cabin Management / Intercommunication Controller
equipment.location: Cabin network controllers and distributed cabin electronics
equipment.purpose: Coordinates cabin lighting, passenger signs, attendant functions and cabin-system data.
equipment.redundancy: Distributed cabin nodes and local control often limit failures to sections rather than the entire cabin.
equipment.failureEffect: Cabin functions degrade by zone; safety-significant functions may have independent hardwired backups.

equipment.name: Central Maintenance Computer
equipment.location: Avionics bay / integrated modular avionics partition
equipment.purpose: Collects fault messages, built-in-test results and maintenance data from aircraft systems.
equipment.redundancy: May be dual or hosted redundantly, but loss primarily affects maintenance diagnostics rather than immediate control.
equipment.failureEffect: Maintenance troubleshooting and fault recording capability is reduced; flight functions continue independently.

equipment.name: Aircraft Data Network Switches / Routers
equipment.location: Avionics racks and distributed network nodes
equipment.purpose: Routes deterministic or conventional digital data between avionics and information-system domains.
equipment.redundancy: Safety-critical networks are commonly dual-path or segregated with redundant switches/links.
equipment.failureEffect: A single network path loss is normally tolerated; multiple failures can isolate avionics functions or trigger reversion modes.

equipment.name: Nitrogen Generation System / Air Separation Modules
equipment.location: Center fuselage or wing-body fairing near fuel-system interfaces
equipment.purpose: Generates nitrogen-enriched air to reduce flammability of selected fuel-tank ullage spaces.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple air-separation modules may be installed; system availability philosophy is type-specific.
equipment.failureEffect: Tank-inerting capability degrades; operational/maintenance consequences depend on certification design.

equipment.name: Auxiliary Power Unit
equipment.purpose: Provides independent electrical and pneumatic power, primarily for ground operation and backup/start support.
equipment.redundancy: The APU is itself an alternate source to engines/ground power; it is normally a single unit.
equipment.failureEffect: Removes a major independent electrical/pneumatic backup and can affect dispatch/ETOPS capability depending on aircraft and route.

equipment.name: APU Electronic Control Box
equipment.location: APU compartment or aft electronics bay
equipment.purpose: Controls APU starting, fuel metering, speed, temperature protection and automatic shutdown logic.
equipment.redundancy: Usually a single dedicated controller with internal monitoring; APU is non-primary propulsion so aircraft-level redundancy comes from main engines/systems.
equipment.failureEffect: APU becomes unavailable or shuts down automatically.

equipment.name: Passenger / Cargo Door Indication & Control Units
equipment.location: Door mechanisms with central indication in avionics/cockpit
equipment.purpose: Monitors door latch/lock status and, where powered, controls door actuation or assist functions.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple proximity switches and independent latch/lock features prevent a single indication fault from representing the full physical barrier.
equipment.failureEffect: Door may be inhibited from dispatch or require manual operation/verification.

equipment.name: Full Authority Digital Engine Control
equipment.purpose: Controls engine fuel flow, variable geometry, starting and protection to meet commanded thrust safely.
equipment.redundancy: Dual-channel FADEC/EEC architecture with independent power/data paths is standard practice on modern large turbofans.
equipment.powerSource: Engine permanent-magnet alternator and/or aircraft electrical backup
equipment.failureEffect: One channel normally hands over to the other; total control loss can lead to engine shutdown or fixed/degraded control depending on design.

equipment.name: Hydromechanical Fuel Unit / Fuel Metering Unit
equipment.purpose: Meters high-pressure fuel to the combustor under FADEC command and provides hydraulic actuation fuel for engine controls.
equipment.redundancy: Normally one metering unit per engine; aircraft-level propulsion redundancy comes from multiple engines, while internal fail-safe features protect the engine.
equipment.failureEffect: Can cause thrust-control degradation, rollback or engine shutdown.

equipment.name: Ignition Exciters / Igniter Plugs
equipment.purpose: Provides high-energy sparks for engine start, relight and selected adverse-weather operation.
equipment.redundancy: Two independent ignition channels/plugs per engine are common.
equipment.failureEffect: One channel loss usually leaves alternate ignition; dual-channel loss prevents normal start/relight.

equipment.name: Variable Stator / Variable Bleed Valve Actuators
equipment.purpose: Schedules compressor geometry and bleed to maintain stable, efficient compressor operation across the envelope.
equipment.redundancy: Usually one coordinated mechanism per engine with multiple feedback sensors; FADEC detects disagreement and drives protective schedules.
equipment.failureEffect: Can reduce thrust margin, increase surge/stall risk and trigger engine-control reversion or shutdown protection.

equipment.name: Engine Speed / Temperature / Pressure Sensors
equipment.location: Distributed across fan, compressor, combustor and turbine modules
equipment.purpose: Provides FADEC and cockpit with engine health/control parameters such as N1/N2, EGT and pressures.
equipment.redundancy: Critical control parameters commonly use multiple pickups or plausibility checks; redundancy varies by sensed quantity.
equipment.failureEffect: Single sensor loss may invoke synthesized/substitute values or alternate sensors; multiple losses can degrade engine control.

equipment.name: Thrust Reverser Actuation System
equipment.purpose: Deploys blocker doors/translating sleeves after landing to redirect fan flow and supplement wheel braking.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple independent locks, position sensors and command interlocks prevent inadvertent in-flight deployment.
equipment.powerSource: Hydraulic or electrical actuation depending on engine/nacelle
equipment.failureEffect: One reverser may be inoperative with performance/dispatch penalties; unsafe disagreement is inhibited by locking logic.

equipment.name: Engine Oil Tank / Pumps / Scavenge System
equipment.location: Engine accessory gearbox and bearing sumps
equipment.purpose: Lubricates and cools engine bearings/gears and scavenges oil back to the tank.
equipment.redundancy: Multiple scavenge elements and sensors exist, but each engine generally has one integrated oil system; aircraft propulsion redundancy comes from the second engine.
equipment.failureEffect: Low oil pressure or severe oil loss can require engine shutdown.

equipment.name: Air Turbine Starter / Starter System
equipment.purpose: Uses pneumatic or electrical power to accelerate the engine core to self-sustaining speed during start.
equipment.redundancy: One starter per engine; start-air can commonly come from APU, opposite engine crossbleed or ground source.
equipment.powerSource: Pneumatic start air or electrical power
equipment.failureEffect: Affected engine cannot be started normally until starter/start-air source is restored.

equipment.name: Starter Air Valve
equipment.purpose: Meters pneumatic air into the air-turbine starter during engine start.
equipment.redundancy: One valve per engine; multiple pneumatic sources can feed it but the valve itself is normally single.
equipment.failureEffect: Failed closed prevents pneumatic start; failed open requires isolation/protection logic.
